text: The product A × B in a category is characterized by the universal property that:
choices: A × B is just the set of ordered pairs (a, b)
there are injections A → A × B and B → A × B
A × B is isomorphic to the coproduct A + B
for every X with maps f: X → A and g: X → B there is a unique ⟨f,g⟩: X → A × B with π₁∘⟨f,g⟩ = f and π₂∘⟨f,g⟩ = g
explanation: The product is defined by its universal property: projections π₁, π₂ through which any pair of maps out of X factors via a unique mediating morphism ⟨f,g⟩. Option A is only the concrete Set construction, not the definition; injections and a mediating map out of the object describe the coproduct (B); products and coproducts differ in general (C).
